issue.title: Localstack does not work with Testcontainers 1.19.0

repository.name: bootique-aws
repository.description: Bootique integration with AWS Java SDK

issue.body:
Running Localstack (either the old version `0.11.3` or the new `2.2.0`) results in this exception:
```
[main] ERROR tc.localstack/localstack:2.2.0 - Could not start container
com.github.dockerjava.api.exception.InternalServerErrorException: Status 500: 
{"message":"error while creating mount source path '/host_mnt/Users/andrus/.docker/run/docker.sock': 
mkdir /host_mnt/Users/andrus/.docker/run/docker.sock: operation not supported"}
```

This happens on Mac and affects Localstack S3, SECRETSMANAGER and probably all other AWS emulation services. This does not happen in CI. There are a few Docker-side workarounds done via Docker desktop Settings. Either one will work indepdenedntly from each other:

1. Check **"Allow the default Docker socket to be used (requires password)"** checkbox 
2. or under **"Choose file sharing"** select "gRPC Fuse" and uncheck **"Use Virtualization Framework"**

While the issue was actually introduced by Docker Desktop, the permanent fix depends on [Testcontainers](https://github.com/testcontainers/testcontainers-java/issues/7678). So waiting for the new TC release to address this.

issue.title: Resolve strategy to detect the remote docker socket

repository.name: testcontainers-java
repository.description: Testcontainers is a Java library that supports JUnit tests, providing lightweight, throwaway instances of common databases, Selenium web browsers, or anything else that can run in a Docker container.

issue.body:
Currently, if `DockerClientFactory.instance().getRemoteDockerUnixSocketPath()`
is called without resolving the strategy then the remote docker socket
can be invalid, for example, using Docker Desktop for Mac with unchecked
`Allow the default Docker socket to be used` option.

Fixes #7678
